name: Bybit linear BTCUSDT perpetual mark one-minute MACD(12, 26, 9)
description: A causal reading over the fresh Bybit linear BTCUSDT perpetual mark price carried by the `tickers` stream, sampled once per second on the lane decision clock. Each one-second sample holds the venue's latest mark row for up to a 3-second bound (a research default; the premium-index poll lands about every 1.3 seconds and Bybit mark prices carry multi-second gaps), and a mark row 3 seconds or more old is a missing sample, so a stalled poll or an absent mark invalidates the bar spanning it and re-warms the identity. The MACD line is the twelve-bar exponential moving average of the one-minute bar closes minus the twenty-six-bar one, both with smoothing factor alpha equal to two divided by (period plus one) and both seeded with the arithmetic mean of their first `period` closes. The signal line is the nine-bar exponential moving average of the MACD line, seeded with the mean of its first nine values, and the histogram is the MACD line minus the signal line. All three are published scale-free, as basis points of the latest bar close: macd_bps, signal_bps and histogram_bps are the respective price-unit values divided by that close, times ten thousand. The twelve, twenty-six and nine lengths are the standard Appel parameters and are initial research defaults that require empirical calibration; the exponential-moving-average recursion is not a heuristic threshold. One-minute bars are closed on the lane decision clock at minute boundaries from the one-second sample series: open is the first sample of the minute, high and low its extrema, close its last sample. A bar that is missing any one-second sample is invalid; the missing sample breaks continuity, every retained bar and every smoothed state derived from them is discarded, and the bar warm-up restarts from the next whole bar. Nothing is bridged across a gap. Ready once thirty-five contiguous one-minute bars have closed: the twenty-six-bar average seeds on bar twenty-six and the nine-bar signal average then needs nine MACD values. Decimal outputs are rounded to eight places using round-half-to-even. Every reading is causal: it reads only samples at or before the decision it is published on. E47 (USD quoting): this identity quotes in USD and publishes no price, notional or quote-denominated cost field — its outputs are basis-point ratios, indices, counts and timestamps, which are quote-currency neutral — so nothing is converted and no usdt_usd_rate is published. quote_currency is the constant "usd". Bybit inputs are rights-gated (`signals/knowledge/RIGHTS-LEDGER.md`): the lane is built and tested to the adopted standard, and its runtime refuses to start unless the environment allow-list `SIGNALS_ENABLED_VENUES` names `bybit`. Adopted in the C3a TA pack (ruling E51, 2026-09-04): the seven technical-analysis identities are published on every price venue we carry, computed from the venue's own one-second sample ring by the shared `crates/btc-signals/src/ta.rs` helper, so every scope runs byte-identical arithmetic and only the sample series differs.
